v14s.imdb.template: Did the writer of this IMDb movie review rate the film positively or negatively?
v14s.imdb.state_kind: one full English user review of a film from IMDb, HTML line breaks restored as newlines; reviews over 4,000 characters are not used
v14s.imdb.answer_meaning: options negative / positive: the class of the rating the writer gave (<= 4/10 negative, >= 7/10 positive; neutral ratings are not in the dataset)

v14s.fpb.template: From an investor's point of view, is this sentence from financial news likely to have a negative, neutral or positive influence on the stock price of the company it concerns?
v14s.fpb.state_kind: one English sentence from financial news about a (mostly Finnish, OMX Helsinki listed) company
v14s.fpb.answer_meaning: a soft distribution over negative / neutral / positive: the annotators' (5-8 finance-trained) majority label, weighted by the published agreement bracket, the remainder on the adjacent class

v14s.tweeteval_irony.state_kind: one English tweet from the TweetEval benchmark, user mentions anonymised as @user
v14s.tweeteval_irony.answer_meaning: options non_irony / irony: the SemEval-2018 Task 3 subtask A label (Van Hee et al.), manually annotated; the #irony/#sarcasm/#not query hashtags were removed by the task organisers

v14s.stance_hillary.template: What stance does the author of this tweet take toward Hillary Clinton?
v14s.stance_hillary.state_kind: one English tweet from the TweetEval benchmark, user mentions anonymised as @user; the target need not be named in the tweet
v14s.stance_hillary.answer_meaning: options none / against / favor: the SemEval-2016 Task 6 stance label toward the target 'Hillary Clinton' -- favor = the author supports it, against = the author opposes it, none = neutral or no clue. Stance toward the target, not the tweet's sentiment

v14s.poem_sentiment.template: What sentiment does this line of poetry convey?
v14s.poem_sentiment.state_kind: one verse (a single line) of an English poem from Project Gutenberg
v14s.poem_sentiment.answer_meaning: options negative / positive / no_impact / mixed: the Gutenberg Poem Dataset label (Sheng & Uthus 2020), expert-annotated per verse

v14s.tfns.template: Is this finance-related tweet bearish, neutral or bullish about the company, asset or market it discusses?
v14s.tfns.state_kind: one English finance-news tweet, often with a $TICKER and a t.co link
v14s.tfns.answer_meaning: options Bearish / Neutral / Bullish: the dataset's annotated sentiment label (LABEL_0 Bearish, LABEL_1 Bullish, LABEL_2 Neutral)

v14s.stance_feminist.template: What stance does the author of this tweet take toward the feminist movement?
v14s.stance_feminist.state_kind: one English tweet from the TweetEval benchmark, user mentions anonymised as @user; the target need not be named in the tweet
v14s.stance_feminist.answer_meaning: options none / against / favor: the SemEval-2016 Task 6 stance label toward the target 'Feminist Movement' -- favor = the author supports it, against = the author opposes it, none = neutral or no clue. Stance toward the target, not the tweet's sentiment

v14s.sst5.template: How negative or positive is the sentiment of this sentence from a movie review?
v14s.sst5.state_kind: one sentence from a Rotten Tomatoes movie review snippet (Stanford Sentiment Treebank train split), detokenised
v14s.sst5.answer_meaning: a soft distribution over the five SST classes: the share of the sentence's annotators (usually 3) whose own 25-point slider value falls in each class under SST's published cut-offs

v14s.amazon_polarity.template: Did the writer of this Amazon review rate the product positively or negatively?
v14s.amazon_polarity.state_kind: the body of one English Amazon product review (the title is removed)
v14s.amazon_polarity.answer_meaning: options negative / positive: the class of the writer's star rating (1-2 negative, 4-5 positive; 3-star reviews are not in the dataset)

v14s.tweeteval_sentiment.template: What is the overall sentiment of this tweet?
v14s.tweeteval_sentiment.state_kind: one English tweet from the TweetEval benchmark, user mentions anonymised as @user
v14s.tweeteval_sentiment.answer_meaning: options negative / neutral / positive: the SemEval-2017 Task 4A message-level sentiment label (Rosenthal et al.), crowd-annotated

v14s.tweeteval_offensive.template: Does this tweet contain offensive language or a targeted offense?
v14s.tweeteval_offensive.state_kind: one English tweet from the TweetEval benchmark, user mentions anonymised as @user; URLs written as URL
v14s.tweeteval_offensive.answer_meaning: options non-offensive / offensive: the OLID level-A label (OffensEval 2019, Zampieri et al.)

v14s.tweeteval_emotion.template: Which emotion best represents the mental state of the author of this tweet?
v14s.tweeteval_emotion.state_kind: one English tweet from the TweetEval benchmark, user mentions anonymised as @user
v14s.tweeteval_emotion.answer_meaning: options anger / joy / optimism / sadness: the SemEval-2018 Task 1 (Affect in Tweets) E-c emotion for tweets carrying one of these four, as TweetEval selects them

v14s.stance_abortion.answer_meaning: options none / against / favor: the SemEval-2016 Task 6 stance label toward the target 'Legalization of Abortion' -- favor = the author supports it, against = the author opposes it, none = neutral or no clue. Stance toward the target, not the tweet's sentiment

Stance toward the target, not the tweet's sentiment

v14s.claim_stance.template: Does this claim support or contest the debate motion?
v14s.claim_stance.state_kind: a JSON object: a debate motion ('This house ...') and one claim about it, a sentence taken from Wikipedia
v14s.claim_stance.answer_meaning: options PRO / CON: the IBM Debater Claim Stance label (Bar-Haim et al. 2017), expert-annotated stance of the claim toward the motion
